If the sending operand is a data item, ... b. If the sending operand is a figurative constant, ... c. If the sending operand is an alphanumeric or national literal, ...
findings.markdown_says:
3\. When the sending operand is described as alphanumeric or national, ...

   a. If the sending operand is a data item, ...

   b. If the sending operand is a figurative constant, ...

   c. If the sending operand is an alphanumeric or national literal, ...

   c) When a receiving item is described as alphabetic, ...
findings.why_it_matters: In MOVE general rule 4b the printed page nests items a.-c. under item 3. (they are the characteristics of the alphanumeric/national sending operand); the markdown puts a.-c. at the same indentation as 1.-3. and as the parent-level c) and d), so the sub-items are detached from item 3 and read as siblings of it.

findings.why_it_matters: Table 18 prints Numeric-edited with no category of its own and splits it into '— if usage is display' -> Alphanumeric and '— if usage is national' -> National. The markdown merges the two sub-rows into one line and drops the blank, so the lines pair positionally as Numeric-edited -> Alphanumeric and the merged usage line -> National: the category of HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE moved to a numeric-edited item of usage national reads as Alphanumeric.
